commit_message:
avcodec/bsf/extract_extradata: remove extradata blocks from supported LCEVC NALUs

Given we rewrite these NALUs to remove the encoded data blocks to export as extradata,
we need to do the inverse to remove SC, GC and AI blocks to export as filtered data in
packes.

Signed-off-by: James Almer <jamrial@gmail.com>

fix_commit_message:
avcodec/bsf/extract_extradata: Replace incorrect size accounting

Fixes: out of array writes
Fixes: 492054712/clusterfuzz-testcase-minimized-ffmpeg_BSF_EXTRACT_EXTRADATA_fuzzer-5705993148497920

Found-by: continuous fuzzing process https://github.com/google/oss-fuzz/tree/master/projects/ffmpeg
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix f84c859ec54d on top of intro 863c748144a1 via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (BufferOverflow): The LCEVC extradata extraction path in libavcodec/bsf/extract_extradata.c (extract_extradata_lcevc) computed the size of the extracted extradata and the filtered packet data incorrectly. write_lcevc_nalu() returns bytestream2_tell_p(pbc), an absolute cursor position within the output PutByteContext after processing a single NAL unit, rather than the number of bytes newly written by that call. The refactor in commit 863c748144 changed the code so that this absolute-position return value was repeatedly added into a running total (*size += ret; filtered_size += ret;) across the loop over NAL units, causing the tracked size to be inflated far beyond the number of bytes actually written and beyond the size of the buffers that were allocated based on a separate (correct) pre-pass calculation. The inflated size value is later used by the caller (extract_extradata_filter) to compute an offset for zero-padding the extradata buffer (memset(extradata + extradata_size, 0, AV_INPUT_BUFFER_PADDING_SIZE)), and is also stored directly as pkt->size for the filtered packet data. Both usages write/interpret memory beyond the true bounds of the allocated buffers, resulting in out-of-array (heap buffer overflow) writes, as found by OSS-Fuzz. Root cause: write_lcevc_nalu()'s return value (bytestream2_tell_p, an absolute position in the shared PutByteContext) was misused as an incremental per-NAL size delta and summed cumulatively across iterations, producing a grossly inflated total size that no longer matches the number of bytes actually written or the size of the allocated buffer.
